question.text: An employee with basic salary of Rs. 60,000 and DA of Rs. 15,000 has been contributing to EPF for 8 years. She now wishes to take a partial withdrawal for purchasing a house. What is the salary-based ceiling that applies to her house-purchase EPF withdrawal?

answer.text: 36 months of basic wages and dearness allowance (i.e., 36 × Rs. 75,000 = Rs. 27,00,000)
24 months of basic wages and dearness allowance (i.e., 24 × Rs. 75,000 = Rs. 18,00,000)

explanation.text: The Logic: For house purchase or construction, EPF rules permit withdrawal of the least of: 36 months of basic wages plus DA, the total EPF balance (employee plus employer share) with interest, and the total cost. The salary-based ceiling is 36 months of basic plus DA, which here is 36 × Rs. 75,000 = Rs. 27,00,000. The Trap: The 24-month figure applies to land purchase only, not house construction/purchase. Candidates often miss that 36 months is only one of three limiting conditions — the actual withdrawal is the least of all three. Note: Always confirm whether the client is purchasing land alone or a house, since the salary-based ceiling differs (24 months vs 36 months), and also verify five years of EPF membership.
